name: Pricing-Reversal Watch
description: A dated, per-provider evidence trail of AI API price and spec changes — rescinded increases, price cuts, renames, and quiet moves, each with the vendor's own words and a pinned capture receipt.
data_source: Vendor pricing pages and changelogs — Anthropic (docs + boundary page), DeepSeek (Models & Pricing + API changelog); OpenAI documented gap (HTTP 403)
records: 17 Anthropic model rows, 2 DeepSeek models x 2 rate bands, 5 change events, 5 capture receipts, 10 verified quotes
detail: Each change event lists announced/observed/confirmed/effective dates, the before -> after values, and verbatim evidence: vendor quotes linked to raw HTML captures pinned by SHA-256, with monitoring notes kept separate and labeled. Featured trail: Claude Sonnet 5's scheduled $3/$15 increase cancelled before it took effect ($2/$10 now standard); DeepSeek's August peak/off-peak escalation ($0.14 -> $0.22 cache-miss) and the September V4.1-Flash price reduction ($0.22 -> $0.15), plus the V4 Pro continuation notice and legacy-name retirement. Fetch failures are recorded with transport errors; vendors without a capture are documented gaps, never clean. Build-time quote verification fails closed.
asymmetry: AI API customers can see current prices but rarely the trajectory: promotional cuts get press, while reversals, rescinded increases, context-window changes, and renames arrive as a changelog line or not at all. Someone mid-migration or deciding to stay on a model family cannot answer 'did this go up, and did it come back down?' without re-reading changelogs. This watch keeps each change with its date and the vendor's own words, so a cancelled increase is as legible as a discount.
pipeline_note: Multi-transport fetch (urllib -> curl) with per-source 60s wall-clock deadlines; raw captures committed with SHA-256 receipts; curated event layer whose quotes are verified against captures at build time (fail closed); monitoring notes distinguished from vendor quotes; documented gaps for unreachable vendors; static site, no backend.
